propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Infirmitatem nostram respice, omnipotens Deus: et, quia pondus propriae
actionis gravat, beatorum Martyrum tuorum Fabiani et Sebastiani intercessio
gloriosa nos protegat. Per Dominum nostrum.

refused.hebrew-unnumbered-titles: English Bibles divide Psalm 126 differently from the Hebrew numbering, and no verse-for-verse correspondence is recorded for it

provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 42-45; antecedent Tours: Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam), printed p. 511; artifact PDF p. 625 (text layer, column-correct -raw extraction)
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: conclusion length differs: the 1962 prints "Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate."; the antecedent prints "Per Dominum. Communio. Luc. 6, 18 et 19. Mul"; accents, ae/oe ligatures and word division differ throughout; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer and its pointing cannot be trusted at comma level. Corroboration: 1862 at text-layer lines 56268-56280 (printed p. 389), alignment 0.74; 1604 at lines 54421-54430, alignment 0.59 (degraded-latin; corroboration only); 1570 at lines 48491-48518, alignment 0.57 (degraded-latin; corroboration only). Recorded limitation: The 1962 reading was settled on the facsimile page image; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer only and its letterforms and pointing were not verified on a page image (the 1862's images are not available to this lane, and the Mame's were not rendered for this entry). What was NOT checked: the Benziger conformed printing was used only as a boundary check on the extraction, never as a reading; no attempt was made to establish which of several possible loci in the antecedent is the 'original' one, since an order is not a contribution. This oration is one the Missal draws from a Common; the antecedent witness may print it at the Common, at another saint's day, or at both. That is a difference of position, not of words.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Hostias tibi, Domine, beatorum Martyrum tuorum Fabiani et Sebastiani dicatas
meritis, benignus assume: et ad perpetuum nobis tribue provenire subsidium.
Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat
in unitate.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Refecti participatione muneris sacri, quaesumus, Domine Deus noster: ut,
cujus exsequimur cultum, intercedentibus sanctis Martyribus tuis Fabiano et
Sebastiano, sentiamus effectum. Per Dominum.
